title: iperf3: add dissector support
description:
iPerf3 is quite different from iPerf2 and so requires its own dissector.
Recognizes "control connection" messages (session cookies, connection
request refusal, etc) and data (labeled with its length, UDP messages
have their sequence number parsed)

It registers with TCP and UDP port 5201, which is unused by any other
dissector in Wireshark.

`cookie` is declared on the stack. It needs to be duplicated to `wmem_file_scope()` before inserting in a map of that scope. (See #19354)
True, I need to fix this.

I get a warning on this line on a 32-bit Raspberry Pi.
```
[69/2013] Building C object epan/dissectors/CMakeFiles/dissectors.dir/packet-iperf3.c.o
../epan/dissectors/packet-iperf3.c: In function 'udp_info_hash':
../epan/dissectors/packet-iperf3.c:132:26: warning: cast to pointer from integer of different size [-Wint-to-pointer-cast]
  132 |     return g_direct_hash((void *)*((const uint64_t *)a));
      |                          ^
```

Since `a` is being used as a pointer to a `uint64_t`, instead of being stored directly with `GUINT_TO_POINTER`, `g_direct_hash` isn't correct and it could just be `g_int64_hash(a)` for the hash (and above, `g_int64_equal`; in fact, it's a little unnecessary to define `udp_info_[equals|hash]` in the first place, though perhaps they could be changed in the future). As it is, different memory addresses that point to the same 64 bit value will hash differently.

OTOH, since the `uint64_t` is assigned from `pinfo->num`, which is 32 bit, the whole part could be rewritten with a `uint32_t` and `GUINT_TO_POINTER` and direct hasing instead of using a `uint64_t`.

> OTOH, since the `uint64_t` is assigned from `pinfo->num`, which is 32 bit, the whole part could be rewritten with a `uint32_t` and `GUINT_TO_POINTER` and direct hasing instead of using a `uint64_t`.

Yes - until we decide to support more than 4294967295 frames in a capture (yes, it's an odd number, because frame numbers start at 1, and 0 is used in several places for "no frame number known"), there's no reason to assign `pinfo->num` to a 64-bit integer.

So I didn't write this part of the code, but it seems to have to be rewritten also. The original author was determined to use 64 bit for everything, so there you have it. Let's see how to overhaul this.
